title: The Battle of the Trench (Ghazwat al-Khandaq / Al-Ahzab)
app_target: 3D Seerah model in the seerah-models series: interactive 3D scenes and a battle timeline, no narration or article

spine_source.work: Raheeq al-Makhtum (MSA NIU English ed.), Saifur Rahman al-Mubarakpuri, trans. Issam Diab (Dar-us-Salam)
spine_source.file: data/raw/page_195.txt ... page_203.txt (extracted text, print page = source page)
spine_source.citation_format: Raheeq al-Makhtum (MSA NIU English ed.), p. N

conventions.block_tagging: All ledger entries are HISTORY. The model ships no article, narration, captions or info cards; labels carry names and counts only.
conventions.honorifics: The Prophet is referenced as 'the Prophet (PBUH)' in any text; Companions carry (RA). No figural depiction of the Prophet (PBUH) or of any identifiable named person.
conventions.quote_cap: Direct on-screen quotes are short; Qur'an anchors are fetched live from api.alquran.cloud and the exact text is recorded below.
conventions.no_harmonization: DISPUTED entries display ranges or both versions. UNKNOWN is never rendered.
conventions.secondary_sirah: Ibn Hisham/Ibn Ishaq-derived detail is cited as it appears in Raheeq; no full translation is owned locally.

grading_policy.CERTAIN: >= 2 independent sources, at least one canonical (Quran > Sahih Bukhari/Muslim > other canonical collections > sirah Ibn Hisham/Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Sa'd, al-Tabari > modern critical works). Raheeq al-Makhtum alone never certifies.
grading_policy.REPORTED: Solid single-chain sirah/hadith detail; accurate to attribute but from one lineage or a modern retelling only; rendered with no certainty implied.
grading_policy.DISPUTED: Transmitted variants conflict; the model must show a range or both versions, never one figure.
grading_policy.UNKNOWN: Cannot be verified from owned + live sources; never rendered.

render_as_policy.solid: Canonical or >= 2 independent sources; safe as a primary on-screen fact.
render_as_policy.approx: Reported or contested detail; render visually/ambiguously, no certainty implied.
render_as_policy.range: DISPUTED counts; show the range, never a single figure.

entries.claim: After their exile, about twenty chiefs of the Jews of Banu Nadir went to Makkah and incited Quraysh, Kinanah and the tribes of Tihama to a confederate war against the Prophet (PBUH); the same delegation went to Ghatfan and the eastern tribes, who agreed to join.

sources.quote: Twenty chiefs of the Jews with some celebrities of Bani Nadir went to Makkah to negotiate an unholy alliance with Quraish

entries.notes: Sirah framing for the coalition; no figure counted on screen.

entries.claim: Quraysh, Kinanah and their allies from Tihama raised four thousand men under Abu Sufyan; the eastern tribes of Banu Saleem, Ghatfan and Bani Murrah joined, and the confederate army gathered before Madinah numbered about ten thousand.

sources.quote: four thousand men under the leadership of Abu Sufyan ... a great army of ten thousand fighters
when armies came to [attack] you

entries.notes: The Qur'an attests the armies, not the count. The model states 'about 10,000' and 'Quraysh 4,000' as the spine gives them.

entries.claim: The Prophet (PBUH) called a council to plan the defence of Madinah; Salman al-Farisi (RA) proposed digging a trench as the Persians did in siege warfare, and the plan was adopted.

sources.quote: it was agreed, on the proposal of an honourable Companion, Salman Al-Farisi, to dig trenches as defensive lines

entries.notes: The model's spine: the trench is the act that defines the battle.

entries.claim: The Muslims dug the trench in parties: forty yards were allocated to each group of ten, and they worked by day and returned home in the evening for several days until the trench was complete before the enemy arrived.

sources.quote: Forty yards was allocated to each group of ten to dig ... they used to work on it during the day, and go back home in the evening

entries.notes: The digging beat; no dimensions beyond the spine are rendered.

entries.claim: The northern side of Madinah was its most vulnerable approach, the other sides being protected by mountains and palm orchards; the Prophet (PBUH) understood that the Confederates would march that way and ordered the trench on that side.

sources.quote: The northern part of Madinah was the most vulnerable, all the other sides being surrounded by mountains and palm tree orchards

entries.notes: Defines the model's axes: open northern approach, Madinah and its groves behind the Muslim line.

entries.claim: The Confederate army camped in the vicinity of Madinah at places called al-Asyal and Uhud; the Muslims, three thousand strong, came out and entrenched at Sila' mountain with the trench standing between them and the enemy.

sources.quote: places called Al-Asyal and Uhud ... They entrenched themselves in Sila‘ Mountain with the trench standing as a barrier between them and the disbelievers

entries.notes: The model's two camps and the mountain at the Muslim rear.

entries.claim: When the believers saw the confederate companies they said, 'This is what Allah and His Messenger had promised us, and Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth,' and it increased them in faith.

sources.quote: And when the believers saw ‘Al- Ahzab’ (the confederates), they said ...
This is what Allah and His Messenger had promised us

entries.notes: The verse is quoted by the spine at this point.

entries.claim: The Muslim force that came out against the Confederates numbered three thousand, with the Prophet (PBUH) at their head.

sources.quote: Three thousand Muslims, with Muhammad [pbuh] at their head, came out to encounter the idolaters

entries.notes: The model shows the 3,000 as three battalions without naming commanders the spine does not name for this battle.

entries.claim: The Confederates were surprised by the trench, a stratagem unknown in Arabia before; unable to break through, they laid siege, probed for a crossing, and exchanged arrows and skirmishes with the Muslims.

sources.quote: a wide trench, a new stratagem unknown in Arabia before ... To deter their enemies ... the Muslims hurled arrows, and engaged in skirmishes

entries.notes: The siege is a standoff; the model does not stage a general engagement.

entries.claim: The battle of the Trench took place in the fifth year Hijri; the siege of Madinah began in Shawwal and ended in Dhul Qa'dah, lasting over a month.

sources.quote: The battle of the Trench took place in the fifth year Hijri ... it lasted for over a month

entries.notes: The model's date line. Other transmitted durations are not in the owned spine and are not shown.

entries.claim: A group of Quraysh fighters led by Amr ibn Abd Wudd, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl and Dirar ibn al-Khattab worked its way through the trench; their horsemen took the marshy ground between the trench and Sila' mountain.

sources.quote: a group of fighters led by ‘Amr bin ‘Abd- e- Wudd, ‘Ikrima bin Abi Jahl and Dirar bin Al- Khattab, should work its way through the trench ... captured a marshy area between the trench and Sila‘ Mountain

entries.notes: The narrow crossing is the model's eastern pass; the marsh is a landmark.

entries.claim: Amr ibn Abd Wudd challenged the Muslims to single combat; Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) was sent against him, and after a short fierce fight Ali killed him, obliging the others to withdraw in panic.

sources.quote: ‘Amr challenged the Muslims to a duel, and ‘Ali bin Abi Talib was deputed. After a short but fierce engagement, ‘Ali killed ‘Amr

entries.notes: Staged as two standards at the crossing, one falling; no named figure and no gore.

entries.claim: Sa'd ibn Mu'adh (RA) was struck by an arrow that pierced an artery; he asked Allah either to let him live for more fighting or to take him after revenge on Banu Qurayza. He died of the wound after the siege.

sources.quote: Sa‘d bin Mu‘adh was shot by an arrow that pierced his artery

entries.notes: Recorded, never staged as a body; the line's loss is told by the quiet and the label.

entries.claim: Huyai ibn Akhtab, chief of Banu Nadir, went to Ka'b ibn Asad, chief of Banu Qurayza, and persuaded him to break his pact with the Prophet (PBUH) and join the Confederates.

sources.quote: Huyai ... went on in this manner until he later managed to win Ka‘b to his side and persuade him to break his covenant with the Muslims

entries.notes: The model shows the Qurayza fort and the broken pact, never a named figure.

entries.claim: After breaking the pact, Banu Qurayza began attacking the isolated garrisons holding the women and children of the Muslims; Safiyya bint Abdul Muttalib (RA) killed a lurking man with a bar of wood while Hassan ibn Thabit was in the fort.

sources.quote: I took a bar of wood, went down and struck the Jew to death

entries.notes: Rendered as the walls and the guarded quarter; no figure for Safiyya (RA).

entries.claim: The Prophet (PBUH) sent Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, Sa'd ibn Ubada, Abdullah ibn Rawaha and Khawat ibn Jubair (RA) to investigate the news of the breach; they found it true and Banu Qurayza openly renouncing the pact.

sources.quote: the four men discovered that the news was true and that the Jews announced openly that no pact of alliance existed any longer

entries.notes: The covenant phase's turn.

entries.claim: The believers were tried and shaken: the Confederates came from above and below, eyes shifted, and hearts reached the throats.

sources.quote: And when the eyes grew wild and the hearts reached to the throats
when they came at you from above you and from below you
There the believers were tested and shaken with a severe shaking

entries.notes: The mood of the covenant beat; no figure for the Prophet (PBUH).

entries.claim: The hypocrites called the promise a delusion and a faction asked permission to return home, saying their houses were unprotected, though they were not.

sources.quote: The hypocrites taunted them with having indulged in delusive hopes
Allah and His Messenger did not promise us except delusion
O people of Yathrib, there is no stability for you [here], so return [home]

entries.notes: Ledger and label only; no individual shown leaving.

entries.claim: The Prophet (PBUH) wrapped himself in his robe and meditated on the perfidy of Banu Qurayza, then announced good tidings of victory and sent fighters back to Madinah to guard the women and children.

sources.quote: he rose to his feet saying: 'Allâh is Great. Hearken you Muslims, to Allâh’s good tidings of victory and support.'

entries.notes: The Prophet (PBUH) is never depicted; his station is a standard. The guard detachment is a small band moving south.

entries.claim: The Prophet (PBUH) considered giving the chiefs of Ghatfan a third of Madinah's fruit crops to buy peace; Sa'd ibn Mu'adh and Sa'd ibn Ubada (RA) advised against it, saying they had no need of such a course now that Allah had honoured them with Islam, and the Prophet (PBUH) set it aside.

sources.quote: if it is a new course you want to follow just to provide security for us then we don’t need it

entries.notes: Ledger only; not staged.

entries.claim: Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud, a man of Ghatfan who had embraced Islam secretly, offered his help; with the Prophet's (PBUH) permission he moved between Banu Qurayza, Quraysh and Ghatfan, inciting each to distrust the others; the allies began to demand hostages, and suspicion undermined the coalition.

sources.quote: A man from the tribe of Ghatfan called Na‘im bin Mas‘ud ... asked the Prophet [pbuh] to order him do anything that might benefit the Muslims

entries.notes: Shown as the enemy camp's standards drawing apart; no figure.

entries.claim: The Prophet (PBUH) invoked Allah against the Confederates: 'O Allah, You are quick in account, You are the sender of the Book, we beseech You to defeat the confederates.'

sources.quote: we beseech You to defeat the confederates

entries.notes: Ledger and the quiet of the line; never a figure for the Prophet (PBUH).

entries.claim: Allah answered: a wind, rain and cold wearied the Confederates, blew down their tents and overturned their cooking vessels; the Qur'an records the wind and unseen hosts.

sources.quote: forces of nature — wind, rain and cold wearied them, tents were blown down, cooking vessels and other equipage overthrown
We sent upon them a wind and armies [of angels] you did not see

entries.notes: The storm is staged as weather and tents, never as figures of angels.

entries.claim: On that cold night the Prophet (PBUH) sent Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman (RA) to find news of the enemy; he found them preparing to leave, unable to achieve their aim.

sources.quote: That very cold night the Messenger of Allâh [pbuh] despatched Hudhaifa bin Al-Yaman to hunt around for news about the enemy

entries.notes: Shown as a small standard moving to the enemy camp in the storm.

entries.claim: The Confederates withdrew; Allah repelled those who disbelieved in their rage, and they obtained no good.

sources.quote: He found out that they were preparing to leave frustrated for their inability to achieve their target
And Allah repelled those who disbelieved, in their rage, not having obtained any good

entries.notes: The camp empties; the trench remains.

entries.claim: With the Confederates gone, the Prophet (PBUH) declared that from then on he would take the initiative in war and would not wait for the land of Islam to be invaded.

sources.quote: thenceforth he would take the initiative in war and would not wait for the land of Islam to be invaded

entries.notes: The reckoning's closing line; no figure for the Prophet (PBUH).

entries.claim: Because the trench stood between the two parties, no direct engagement took place; the fighting was confined to arrows, and the siege claimed six Muslims and ten polytheists, one or two of them killed by the sword.

sources.quote: the fight claimed the lives of a small number of fighters, six Muslims and ten polytheists, one or two killed by sword

entries.notes: The model's casualty label: '6 Muslims · 10 Confederates killed' as the spine gives them.

entries.claim: The siege was a battle of nerves rather than of losses, and one of the most decisive battles of early Islam: it proved that no force, however large, could exterminate the Muslim state in Madinah.

sources.quote: It was in fact a battle of nerves rather than of losses ... one of the most decisive battles in the early history of Islam

entries.notes: The reckoning's meaning; the model states only what the spine says.

entries.claim: The fighting detained the Prophet (PBUH) from some prayers; he prayed the afternoon prayer at Buthan after the sun had set and then the sunset prayer, and he invoked Allah to fill the enemies' houses and graves with fire.

sources.quote: he invoked Allâh’s wrath on his enemies

entries.notes: Recorded for the ledger; not rendered.

entries.claim: A stubborn rock stood in the trench; the Prophet (PBUH) struck it with a spade and it broke, and he spoke of the keys of Syria, Persia and Yemen as he struck.

sources.quote: The Prophet [pbuh] took the spade and struck, and the rock immediately turned into a loose sand dune

entries.notes: A Prophetic sign recorded in the spine; not staged, as the series does not depict the Prophet (PBUH).

entries.claim: Jabir ibn Abdullah's sheep and barley fed the thousand men digging the trench, and a woman's handful of dates increased until they dropped over the Prophet's cloak.

sources.quote: the Prophet [pbuh] gathered all the thousand people engaged in digging the trench and they started to eat until they were all completely full

entries.notes: Recorded for the ledger; not rendered.

entries.claim: After the siege the Prophet (PBUH) marched on Banu Qurayza with three thousand foot and thirty horse; their forts were besieged for twenty-five days, their fighting men were judged by Sa'd ibn Mu'adh (RA), and six to seven hundred were killed; their arms and wealth passed to the Muslims.

sources.quote: a number of Jews between six and seven hundred were beheaded therein ... the siege of Banu Quraiza’s forts lasted for 25 days
And He brought down those who supported them among the People of the Scripture from their fortresses
And He caused you to inherit their land and their homes and their properties

entries.notes: The Qurayza expedition is the sequel in the spine, outside this model's visual scope. The model shows only the broken pact and the fort; the judgment is never staged.

entries.claim: The Prophet (PBUH) remained with the Muslim force at Sila' and directed the defence; his station is marked by a standard and is never a figure.

sources.quote: Three thousand Muslims, with Muhammad [pbuh] at their head ... The Messenger of Allâh, [pbuh] wrapped himself in his robe and began to meditate

entries.notes: The series' depiction rule: the Prophet (PBUH) is never depicted in any form.

entries.claim: The Confederates were a coalition, not one army: Quraysh and their Tihama allies under Abu Sufyan, Ghatfan and the eastern tribes, and the Jewish delegation that had incited them.

sources.quote: Quraish, Kinanah and other allies from Tihama ... From the east there came tribes of Banu Saleem, Ghatfan, Bani Murrah

entries.notes: The model arrays them as three camps with separate standards.

entries.claim: After breaking their pact, Banu Qurayza supplied the Confederates in support of their war against the Muslims, though the attack on the women's garrison had been discouraged.

sources.quote: they, however, went on providing the idolaters with supplies in token of their support against the Muslims

entries.notes: Shown as the fort's gate opening to the enemy side; no figure.

entries.claim: The expedition is called al-Ahzab (the Confederates) in the Qur'an and al-Khandaq (the trench) in the sirah.

sources.quote: Al-Ahzab (the Confederates) Invasion ... The battle of the Trench
when armies came to [attack] you

entries.notes: The page title and brand: Khandaq, the trench; the Qur'anic name is the Confederates.

entries.claim: The confederate army gathered in the vicinity of Madinah at al-Asyal and Uhud, north of the city, where the open approach lay.

sources.quote: settled in the vicinity of Madinah in places called Al- Asyal and Uhud
when they came at you from above you and from below you

entries.notes: The enemy camps are placed on the open northern side; the label says 'the northern approach'.

entries.claim: The horsemen who crossed the trench held the marshy ground between the trench and Sila' until Ali (RA) killed Amr and they withdrew.

sources.quote: their horsemen captured a marshy area between the trench and Sila‘ Mountain ... ‘Ali killed ‘Amr and obliged the others to evacuate in a state of panic

entries.notes: The crossing vignette's cavalry probe.
